Q: There's No Business like Show Business
A: "\"There's No Business Like Show Business\" is an Irving Berlin song, written for the 1946 musical \"Annie Get Your Gun\" and orchestrated by Ted Royal. The song serves as a tongue-in-cheek salute to the glamour and excitement of a life in show business, and is performed in the musical by members of \"Buffalo Bill's Wild West\" Show in an attempt to persuade Annie Oakley to join the production. Q: "What was ""The Hindenburg Line""?"
A: "The Hindenburg Line, also known as the Siegfried Position, was a German defensive position of World War I, built during the winter of 1916\u20131917 on the Western Front, from Arras to Laffaux, near Soissons on the Aisne. It was established as a response to the costly failures of the German offensive at the Battle of Verdun and the Anglo-French offensive at the Battle of the Somme, which had exhausted the German armies. The Hindenburg Line served as a fortified defensive line that the Germans retreated to during the war."
